newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediobanca sets price of convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: Mediobanca sets price of convertible bond.

text.p: Italian merchant bank Mediobanca said it had priced a five-year 915 billion lire bond convertible into shares in insurer Alleanza Assicurazioni at 86.836 percent of nominal value of 15,250 lire.
A Mediobanca statement said this corresponded to an issue price of 13,242.49 lire -- a premium of 12.7 percent to the Alleanza share price on May 21.
Mediobanca said the bonds were convertible into 60 million Alleanza ordinary shares, up from an original 830 billion lire issue convertible into 53 shares.

The bond issue, with an effective yield at maturity of five percent, could be increased further to 68 million shares convertible into a maximum 68 million Alleanza shares if the over allotment option is exercised, the bank said.

Mediobanca is global coordinator for the placement together with joint lead managers Goldman Sachs International and Paribas. Mediobanca said it had asked for the bond to be listed on the Luxembourg stock exchange.
